image.name: DataBank
image.description: DataBank Holdings, Ltd. operates a nationwide digital-infrastructure platform providing colocation, interconnection, cloud, storage, managed security and compliance services to enterprise, cloud, content and technology customers. Founded in Dallas in 2005, DataBank was acquired from Avista by a DigitalBridge-led group in July 2016 and has since expanded through acquisitions, development and multiple recapitalizations. DataBank reported more than 70 data centers in more than 25 markets, 20 interconnection hubs, more than 2,200 customers and more than $1 billion of revenue in May 2026. The current manager-universe ownership roster is DigitalBridge, Swiss Life Asset Managers, IMCO, AustralianSuper, Northleaf Capital Partners, Ardian and CBRE Investment Management. DigitalBridge disclosed a 7.8% continuing stake after the January 2025 secondary. TIAA's Real Estate Account separately disclosed a 14.8% beneficial stake through DigitalBridge Zeus vehicles; DataBank brands that relationship as Nuveen, but it is not evidenced as a Nuveen Infrastructure investment. EDF Invest and TJC are also current investors outside the supplied manager universe. Individual data centers, campuses, interconnection hubs and acquired operating assets remain within the single DataBank platform boundary. No later full sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026.

image.name: Transurban Chesapeake
image.description: Transurban Chesapeake LLC is the concession platform that owns the entities operating the 495, 95 and 395 Express Lanes in Northern Virginia, including the Fredericksburg Extension and 495 NEXT. It develops, finances, operates and maintains dynamically priced express lanes serving motorists, high-occupancy vehicles, buses and permitted commercial traffic in partnership with VDOT. At June 30, 2026, Transurban reported 50% ownership, AustralianSuper 25%, CPP Investments 15% and UniSuper 10%; only AustralianSuper and CPP Investments are tracked infrastructure-manager owners here. The 495 concession covered 26.5 kilometres and the 95/395/FredEx concession 79 kilometres, each running through December 2087. No platform sale, secondary transfer or signed pending exit was identified through August 18, 2026. Chesapeake Partnership and Chesapeake toll road network are aliases for the same manager-level platform; individual roads and extensions are components, not separate PortCos.

image.name: Axium Extendicare LTC II LP
image.description: Axium Extendicare LTC II LP is the Ontario-Manitoba long-term-care ownership platform that succeeded AXR Operating (National) LP and the relevant portion of the former Revera-Axium joint venture. At June 30, 2026, it owned 26 operating homes with 3,502 beds; Axium held 85% through Axium LTC Limited Partnership, while Extendicare held a 15% managed interest and operated the homes. The platform serves residents requiring provincially regulated long-term care and receives operating, management and procurement services from Extendicare. Arbour Heights is a 174-bed Kingston home beneath this platform, not a separate PortCo. The original venture formed in 2017 at 75% Axium and 25% Revera, separated its western assets into an AgeCare-Axium venture in 2022, and became Axium Extendicare LTC II LP when Extendicare acquired Revera's remaining 15% Ontario-Manitoba interest in 2023. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 18, 2026.

image.name: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom
image.description: Axium Aster & Axium Bloom is Axium Infrastructure's combined manager-level investment in two Canadian long-term-care property portfolios. Axium's current portfolio materials report 26 operating facilities and 4,114 beds across Alberta and British Columbia, with cash flows supported by provincially licensed, regulated and funded long-term-care and continuing-care frameworks plus resident co-payments. Axium owns 92.5% of each portfolio; AgeCare owns the 7.5% balance and operates the facilities. Aster began in 2020 as a five-facility, 1,402-bed Alberta partnership at 80% Axium and 20% AgeCare. Bloom traces to the western tranche of the Revera-Axium joint venture that first closed in 2017; Revera sold its remaining 15% interest in certain Alberta and British Columbia homes to AgeCare in 2022. Individual homes are underlying assets, and the separately presented 16-home Ontario Axium Iris portfolio is outside this company boundary. No Axium exit or signed pending sale was identified through August 18, 2026.

image.description: Etobicoke Healthcare Partnership LP is the availability-based design-build-finance-maintain project company for the Etobicoke General Hospital Phase 1 Patient Tower in Toronto, Ontario. image.name: Montreal Gateway Terminals Partnership
aliases: Terminaux Montréal Gateway Société en commandite
image.description: Montreal Gateway Terminals Partnership is a common-user marine container terminal operator at the Port of Montreal. It operates the Cast and Racine terminals as one intermodal platform, providing vessel, yard, reefer, storage, gate and rail/truck-transfer services to global shipping lines and cargo owners serving Canada and the U.S. Midwest and Northeast. The Port of Montreal reports effective handling capacity of 800,000 TEU at Cast and 500,000 TEU at Racine. A consortium led by Fiera Axium Infrastructure acquired 100% of the business from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners on March 5, 2015; Fiera Axium Infrastructure Canada II L.P. was the disclosed Axium vehicle, but Axium's individual stake was not published. Axium's live portfolio continues to list the asset as operational. A 2025 debt refinancing identified FA MGT Limited Partnership as the parent but did not transfer equity. Public evidence reviewed did not support carrying the other 2015 consortium members forward as confirmed active owner rows, and no later sale or signed pending exit was found through August 18, 2026. Termont Montreal, the Port authority, and the individual Cast and Racine terminals are not separate companies within this record.

image.description: Cleco Corporate Holdings LLC is the operating parent within the privately held Cleco Group utility platform, serving Louisiana through Cleco Power and related generation assets. The regulated utility serves approximately 298,000 customers across 24 Louisiana parishes and owns eight generating units with 2,676 MW of rated capacity, supported by transmission and distribution networks and approved tariffs. Macquarie Asset Management, BCI and Manulife completed the take-private acquisition on April 13, 2016 and remain the legal owners; their last publicly confirmed 2020 interests were 53.9%, 36.9% and 9.2%, respectively, while exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. A signed agreement announced April 27, 2026 would sell 100% of Cleco Group to Pine JV Holdings LLC, backed by Stonepeak and Bernhard Capital Partners, but the regulatory proceedings remained open through August 19, 2026, so the existing owners remain active pending closing.

state.attributionRationale: Cleco's April 13, 2016 closing disclosure expressly identifies Macquarie Infrastructure Partners III, L.P. as providing transaction funding alongside the other consortium investors. The March 29, 2017 prospectus identifies MIP Cleco Partners L.P. as the consortium member affiliated with MIP III, and defines MIP III collectively to include its PV partnership. Preserve the existing MIP III fund link and MIP Cleco Partners L.P. legal vehicle; no split or allocation between parallel partnerships or new September 2026 ownership event is inferred.

The March 29, 2017 Cleco prospectus identifies John Hancock Life Insurance Company (U.S.A.) in its Investors definition and describes John Hancock Financial as part of Manulife. It does not identify Manulife Infrastructure Fund I as the underlying investor. Preserve the disclosed insurer vehicle and current unlinked fund state, but remove the unsupported specific-fund assertion. The reviewed evidence does not resolve allocation between insurer capital and any underlying client fund; do not infer a direct-program classification, fund, stake or new ownership event.

BCI's combined Infrastructure and Renewable Resources financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2024 describe a program comprising several funds and structured entities, not one legal investment entity. Note 7 reports Cleco Corporation as an investment held through intermediary corporations. This supports program attribution, not a particular constituent fund or allocation to a named Bolsena vehicle. Preserve bcIMC Como Investment LP and the existing owner identity; no current percentage or September 2026 ownership event is inferred.

image.name: Mosaic Forest Management
image.description: Mosaic Forest Management is a Canadian timberlands and land-management platform overseeing the TimberWest and Island Timberlands interests across Vancouver Island and coastal British Columbia. The business manages sustainable forestry, timber production and related land uses, including renewable-energy, watershed, recreation, real-estate and carbon initiatives. Mosaic launched on November 1, 2018. BCI remains the in-scope infrastructure owner through its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program and reported a 56.1% interest in Mosaic LP at year-end 2025. PSP Investments remains the other legal owner through its Natural Resources mandate; its exact published percentage is not publicly disclosed, and it is not treated as a PSP Infrastructure holding. AIMCo participated at launch but was no longer named in Mosaic's 2024 statutory ownership report, so it is preserved as a former owner with an undisclosed exit date.

image.name: Nexus Water Group, Inc.
image.description: Nexus Water Group, Inc. is a regulated water and wastewater utility platform formed when the U.S. regulated operations of Corix Infrastructure combined with SouthWest Water Company on April 1, 2024. The business operates locally branded systems across the United States and Canada and serves more than 1.3 million people. BCI owns 50.0% through its Infrastructure & Renewable Resources program. The other 50% is held through SWMAC Holdco, producing indirect platform interests of 37.5% for J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Infrastructure Investments Fund and 12.5% for a Munich Re vehicle managed by MEAG. Nexus completed the sale of systems in eight states to American Water on June 1, 2026, while its announced Nevada and Oregon asset sale remained pending; neither transaction is a sponsor sale or platform exit.

milestones.event: The U.S. regulated water and wastewater businesses of Corix Infrastructure and SouthWest Water combined to form Nexus Water Group.
BCI's Corix interests and the IIF/Bazos-backed SouthWest platform completed their combination, establishing the 50% BCI and 50% SWMAC ownership structure.
MEAG completed a 25% investment in predecessor SouthWest Water on behalf of Munich Re, an interest later carried into Nexus through Bazos and SWMAC Holdco.
American Water completed its purchase of Nexus systems in eight states; the transaction was an asset divestiture and did not change ownership of the Nexus platform.
Nexus agreed to sell its Nevada and Oregon systems to California Water Service Group; the asset sale remained pending regulatory approval in the buyer's July 29, 2026 filing.

state.attributionRationale: Filed Tennessee testimony explicitly identifies Infrastructure Investments Fund (IIF) as the investor through IIF Subway Investment LP. The separate CPUC appendix supplies the proposed holding-company chain, and the April 2, 2024 company release confirms closing on April 1. Retain disclosed IIF attribution, the exact existing vehicle and 37.5% indirect stake without treating a calculated indirect percentage as a separately published direct share or making a new September 2026 ownership claim.

BCI's 2025 combined Infrastructure and Renewable Resources statements define a program, not a legal entity, and report Nexus Water Group through intermediary holding corporations at 50.0% in 2025 and 2024. They do not allocate Nexus to a named constituent fund. Preserve the BCI organization, Corix affiliate vehicle and dated stake; use unlinked DIRECT_PROGRAM with no invented Bolsena or other legal-fund allocation.

Filed Tennessee testimony identifies Bazos CIV, L.P. as indirectly owned by Munich Re; MEAG's June 15, 2018 release separately confirms its managed indirect SouthWest investment closed June 14. The CPUC holding-company appendix and existing canonical Nexus receipt bind the continuation, not a new 2018 Nexus ownership period. Attribute the identified Munich Re capital managed by MEAG as DIRECT_PROGRAM, without inventing a named MEAG fund, and preserve the existing 12.5% indirect stake limitation.
